root_cause: The disclosure menu does not close when focus leaves the menu tree, causing the dropdown to remain visible and cover page content after tabbing out.
repair_strategy: Add a focusout listener to the menu element that checks if the related target is outside the menu; if so, and the menu has an open controller, close the controller.
expected_accessibility_effect: When a user tabs out of the navigation dropdown, the dropdown will close, preventing it from obscuring page content.
functional_risks: Potential unintended closure if focus moves to an element that is not a DOM descendant of the menu but is logically part of the menu (e.g., a portal).
If the menu is used as a trigger for non‑menu popups, those popups may close prematurely.
Edge cases where rapid focus shifts could cause flicker, though the containment check mitigates this.
verification_requirements: Tabbing from any menu item to an element outside the menu closes the dropdown (aria-expanded false, submenu hidden).
Moving focus within the menu or into a submenu does not close the dropdown.
Keyboard navigation inside the dropdown (arrow keys, Home, End) continues to work when open.
Clicking the Shop button still opens and closes the dropdown as expected.
